intro: Written after his first trip to England in the winter of 1962–63. The melody and some of the shape come from the English folk song "Scarborough Fair", which he learned from Martin Carthy in London.

lives.title: Learning from Martin Carthy
lives.note: Carthy taught him his arrangement of Scarborough Fair; Dylan built a new song on its frame.

lives.title: Freewheelin'
lives.note: Voice, finger-picked guitar and harmonica. On The Freewheelin' Bob Dylan.

lives.title: Duet with Johnny Cash
lives.note: Sung together in Nashville and used to open Nashville Skyline, Dylan in his new, smoother voice.

lives.title: Back in the set
lives.note: Played in most shows of 2019, Dylan at the piano.

others.note: A stage musical named after the song, built on Dylan's catalogue, opened at the Old Vic and went on to Broadway.
